Title: Weight Loss Stalled? Dieters Underestimate Calories by 47%

Description:
Up to 85% of dieters hit a weight-loss plateau at some point, and it's not about willpower. A classic NEJM study found dieters underreported their actual calorie intake by 47% on average. Losing weight also costs some muscle, which slows resting metabolism (Mayo Clinic). And a year after weight loss, hunger hormones like leptin and ghrelin still hadn't returned to baseline in another NEJM study. Track your food honestly for a week or two, add strength training and enough protein, and consider a short diet break at maintenance calories.
